label: Opposite house
summary: The other house in a relation between two houses, as shown in the dynasty house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the dynasty house window, so the block shows that other house. What exactly counts as opposite (the house that is not the one being viewed) is read from the name, not documented.

label: House relation
summary: The house relation (the standing between two houses) that this item stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the dynasty house window, so that block works on the relation.

label: This relation item
summary: The house relation item itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and by the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls), it passes the object on. Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this level
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the house relation level itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Level description
summary: The description text of a house relation level.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the shared tooltip layout (cooltip).

label: Level flat icon
summary: The flat (simple, unrendered) icon picture of a house relation level.
details: Going by its name and the use of the same name on another type as a texture in the HUD, it is meant to be used as an image. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Level name
summary: The name of a house relation level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the heading of the tooltip for a bar item in the house relations display. Going by the sibling GetNameNoTooltip, this form probably lets the name carry a hover tooltip of its own.

label: Level name, plain
summary: The name of a house relation level as plain text.
details: Vanilla uses it as text in the shared tooltip layout (cooltip). Going by its name, the text carries no hover tooltip.

label: Level effects text
summary: The description text of the parameters of a house relation level.
details: Vanilla puts it under the level's name in the tooltip of a bar item in the house relations display, and also shows it in the shared tooltip layout. What a parameter is here is not documented.

label: Level icon
summary: The rendered icon picture of a house relation level.
details: Vanilla uses it as an image in the dynasty house window and in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Has flat icon
summary: Probably whether the house relation level has a flat icon.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in the game uses it, and the game's documentation lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Has rendered icon
summary: Probably whether the house relation level has a rendered icon.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in the game uses it, and the game's documentation lists its return type as unregistered.

label: This relation level
summary: The house relation level itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Vanilla compares it with another level using ObjectsEqual, to show something only for the level that matches the relation's current level.

label: Access this type
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the house relation type itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Levels of type
summary: Probably the list of levels that this house relation type has.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in the game uses it on this type; the same name on another type (LegitimacyType) appears in legitimacy texts.

label: Type name
summary: The name of a house relation type, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Nothing in the game uses it on this type; the same name is used for names of many other kinds of things.

label: Type name, plain
summary: The name of a house relation type as plain text, without a hover tooltip.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Nothing in the game uses it on this type; the same function name on other types gives names without tooltips.

label: This relation type
summary: The house relation type itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this entry
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the house unity changelog entry itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Entry character
summary: The character linked to a house unity changelog entry.
details: Vanilla writes its name after the date in the changelog line of the character-triggered kind.

label: Entry current stage
summary: The house unity stage type that this changelog entry names as its current one.
details: Vanilla takes the icon of it for the entry in the dynasty house window. Going by the name, it pairs with GetNextHouseUnityStageType; how exactly the two differ is not documented.

label: Entry date
summary: The date of a house unity changelog entry.
details: Vanilla writes it as a string at the start of each changelog line in the house view.

label: Entry description
summary: The description text of a house unity changelog entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of an entry in the dynasty house window.

label: Entry next stage
summary: The house unity stage type that this changelog entry names as its next one.
details: The changelog text shows its name after House Unity changed to. It can be empty: vanilla checks IsValid on it to decide what to show.

label: Entry progress
summary: A whole number for the house unity progress of this changelog entry.
details: Vanilla only compares it with 0, to show one thing when it is above 0 and another when it is 0 or less.

label: This entry
summary: The house unity changelog entry itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this stage
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the house unity stage itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Unity effect text
summary: The text that says how something affects house unity at this stage, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the player (GetPlayer) and shows the result as text in the dynasty house window. Going by the name, it describes how something affects house unity; what the argument changes is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A character. Vanilla passes the player.

label: Stage background
summary: The background picture of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the dynasty house window.

label: Stage description
summary: The description text of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the dynasty house window and in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Stage icon
summary: The icon picture of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in several places of the dynasty house window.

label: Stage key
summary: The key (the script name) of a house unity stage, as text.
details: Vanilla builds an icon name from it in texts about the house's unity stage: @dynasty_house_unity_ followed by the key.

label: Stage modifier text
summary: The text that describes the modifiers of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the dynasty house window. Going by its name, the modifiers are the bonuses and penalties the stage gives.

label: Stage name
summary: The name of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts that say which house unity stage a house is in. Going by the sibling GetNameNoTooltip, this form probably lets the name carry a hover tooltip of its own.

label: Stage name, plain
summary: The name of a house unity stage as plain text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the dynasty house window and in the shared tooltip layout. Going by its name, the text carries no hover tooltip.

label: Stage progress bar
summary: The progress bar picture of a house unity stage.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the dynasty house window.

label: Has background
summary: Probably whether the house unity stage has a background picture.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in the game uses it, and the game's documentation lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Has icon
summary: Probably whether the house unity stage has an icon.
details: Going by its name. Nothing uses it on this type; other types have a HasIcon that the shared tooltip layout checks before showing an icon.

label: Has progress bar
summary: Probably whether the house unity stage has a progress bar picture.
details: Going by its name. Nothing in the game uses it, and the game's documentation lists its return type as unregistered.

label: Stage is valid
summary: Whether the house unity stage is valid.
details: Vanilla combines it with whether the stage is the active one (GUIHouseUnityStage.IsActive), to show different parts of the dynasty house window. What makes a stage invalid is not documented.

label: This stage
summary: The house unity stage itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the dynasty house view to get the decisions that belong to the stage.

label: Access this widget
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the bottom HUD widget itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: This widget
summary: The bottom HUD widget itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this objective
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the HUD ruler objective itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Can estimate progress
summary: Whether the game can estimate how far the ruler objective is completed.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the ruler objective HUD only when it is true.

label: Close
summary: Closes the ruler objective HUD window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked. It is an action, not a value.

label: Advice list
summary: The list of advice entries shown for the ruler objective.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the list a part of the objective window repeats over. What the entries contain is not shown.

label: Decision confirm text
summary: The confirmation text of the decision tied to the ruler objective.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the ruler objective HUD.

label: Decision picture
summary: The picture of the decision linked to the ruler objective.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the ruler objective HUD window.

label: Estimated progress
summary: The estimated completion of the ruler objective, as a number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a progress bar and writes it in a text as Objective N% Complete, so it is a percentage.

label: Open decision details
summary: Opens the detail view of the decision linked to the ruler objective.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked. It is an action, not a value.

label: This objective
summary: The HUD ruler objective itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this window
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the culture hybridization window itself.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

label: Can do hybrid naming list
summary: Whether a hybrid naming list can be made in the culture hybridization window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the naming list part of the window only when it is true.

label: Can have hybrid clothing
summary: Whether the new hybrid culture can have its own mixed clothing style.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the clothing part of the hybridization window only when it is true.

label: Can have hybrid coats of arms
summary: Whether the new hybrid culture can have mixed coats of arms (CoA).
details: Vanilla uses it to show the coat of arms parts of the hybridization window only when it is true.

label: Can hybridize
summary: Whether the player can form the hybrid culture with the current choices.
details: Vanilla enables the button that forms the culture only when it is true, and shows the blockers box in the window when it is false.

label: Can pay cost
summary: Whether the player can pay the cost of forming the hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the window when it is false (Not).

label: Close
summary: Closes the culture hybridization window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked. It is an action, not a value.

label: New culture color
summary: The color chosen for the new hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tint and as a color in the hybridization window. It is a four-part color value.

label: Ethos
summary: Probably an ethos (the cultural mindset) of a culture shown in the hybridization window.
details: Going by its name and by Culture.GetEthos in other texts. Which of the two cultures it means is not known, and nothing uses it on this window.

label: Heritage
summary: Probably a heritage (the cultural family) of a culture shown in the hybridization window.
details: Going by its name and by Culture.GetHeritage in other texts. Which of the two cultures it means is not known, and nothing uses it on this window.

label: Hybridize blockers
summary: The text that lists the reasons why the hybrid culture cannot be formed yet.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the window, and it is the last part of the tooltip of the button that forms the culture.

label: Cost breakdown
summary: The text that breaks the cost of forming the hybrid culture into its parts.
details: Vanilla puts it under the total in the cost tooltip.

label: Cost
summary: The total cost of forming the hybrid culture, as text.
details: Vanilla writes it after Cost: in the window and in the cost tooltip.

label: Innovations gained
summary: The list of innovations the new hybrid culture would discover.
details: Vanilla counts the list with GetDataModelSize for the text You will discover N innovations, and shows the part of the window only when the count is above 0.

label: Language
summary: Probably a language of a culture shown in the hybridization window.
details: Going by its name and by Culture.GetLanguage in other texts. Which of the two cultures it means is not known, and nothing uses it on this window.

label: Left coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms shown on the left side of the hybridization window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of coat of arms blocks in the window.

label: Left holding picture
summary: A picture called the holding texture, shown on the left side of the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the hybridization window, in the buildings choice. What a holding texture shows is read from the name only.

label: Left naming examples
summary: Example names from the naming list of the left side, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the hybridization window.

label: Left portrait picture
summary: A rendered portrait picture for the left side of the hybridization window.
details: Vanilla passes an environment name, a camera name and the widget's screen size, and uses the result as the portrait texture of a widget. The meaning of each argument is read from vanilla's values.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The environment (scene setup) of the picture. Vanilla passes environment_body.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The camera of the picture. Vanilla passes camera_body.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The size of the picture. Vanilla passes the screen size of the widget.

label: Martial pillar
summary: Probably the martial pillar of the culture shown in the window.
details: Going by its name. Nothing uses it on this window; the window shows GetPlayer.GetCulture.GetMartial, and the culture window uses Culture.GetMartial.

label: New culture name
summary: The name the player has typed for the new hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla shows it in the window, and shows the words Choose Name in front while it is empty.

label: Other culture
summary: The other culture shown in the hybridization window, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of blocks in the window. Which culture counts as the other one is not documented; going by the window, the first one is probably the player's.

label: Right coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms shown on the right side of the hybridization window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of coat of arms blocks in the window.

label: Right holding picture
summary: A picture called the holding texture, shown on the right side of the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the hybridization window. What a holding texture shows is read from the name only.

label: Right naming examples
summary: Example names from the naming list of the right side, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the hybridization window.

label: Right portrait picture
summary: A rendered portrait picture for the right side of the hybridization window.
details: Vanilla passes an environment name, a camera name and the widget's screen size, and uses the result as the portrait texture of a widget. The meaning of each argument is read from vanilla's values.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The environment (scene setup) of the picture. Vanilla passes environment_body.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The camera of the picture. Vanilla passes camera_body.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The size of the picture. Vanilla passes the screen size of the widget.

label: Tradition picks left
summary: Probably how many more traditions can still be picked for the hybrid culture.
details: Going by its name and its whole-number return type. Nothing in the game uses it.

label: Tradition picks
summary: The number of traditions picked so far for the hybrid culture, going by the game text.
details: Vanilla writes it in the text Pick up to N traditions from either culture, in parentheses followed by the word selected. The name says total; the text reads like a count of the chosen ones.

label: Traditions
summary: The list of traditions the player can choose from for the hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a part of the window repeats over. Going by the window, each item is a tradition to choose.

label: Vassal conversion window
summary: The part of the window that deals with converting vassals to the new culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the hybridization window. The name is the only hint to its meaning.

label: Has different coat of arms frames
summary: Whether the two cultures have different coat of arms frames.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the hybridization window when it is true. The exact meaning is read from the name.

label: Hybrid clothing chosen
summary: Whether the mixed (hybrid) clothing choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetHybridClothing.

label: Hybrid coats of arms chosen
summary: Whether the mixed (hybrid) coats of arms choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetHybridCoAs.

label: Hybrid naming list chosen
summary: Whether the mixed (hybrid) naming list choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetHybridNamingList.

label: Left buildings chosen
summary: Whether the left side's buildings choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftBuildings. It also checks it together with HasRightBuildings to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Left clothing chosen
summary: Whether the left side's clothing choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftClothing. It also checks it together with HasRightClothing to show parts of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Left coat of arms frame chosen
summary: Whether the left side's coat of arms frame choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftCoAFrame.

label: Left coats of arms chosen
summary: Whether the left side's coats of arms choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftCoAs. It also checks it together with HasRightCoAs to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

summary: Whether the left side's naming list choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftNamingList. It also checks it together with HasRightNamingList to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Left naming style chosen
summary: Whether the left side's naming style choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftNamingStyle. It also checks it together with HasRightNamingStyle to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Left units chosen
summary: Whether the left side's military units choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetLeftUnits. It also checks it together with HasRightUnits to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Has pillar
summary: Whether the given culture pillar is part of the new hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture pillar (CulturePillar.Self) and uses the result as the pressed state of a button and to show parts of the window. SetPillar is the matching action.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture pillar, such as CulturePillar.Self

summary: Whether the right side's buildings choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightBuildings. It also checks it together with HasLeftBuildings to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Right clothing chosen
summary: Whether the right side's clothing choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightClothing. It also checks it together with HasLeftClothing to show parts of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

summary: Whether the right side's coat of arms frame choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightCoAFrame.

summary: Whether the right side's naming list choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightNamingList. It also checks it together with HasLeftNamingList to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

summary: Whether the right side's naming style choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightNamingStyle. It also checks it together with HasLeftNamingStyle to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Right units chosen
summary: Whether the right side's military units choice is selected.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button; the button's click runs SetRightUnits. It also checks it together with HasLeftUnits to show a part of the window when they are not both true, and the exact meaning there is not documented.

label: Has tradition
summary: Whether the given culture tradition is part of the new hybrid culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture tradition (CultureTradition.Self) and shows a part of the window when the result is true. ToggleTradition is the matching action.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a culture tradition, such as CultureTradition.Self

label: Access this illustration

details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The thing the illustration is for. Vanilla passes Character.Self.

details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows the same name on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passing a widget to a window function).

details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the shared dialogs.

label: This popup
summary: The image popup itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Access this tool

details: The import tool belongs to the engine's internal GUI category, not to the playable game. The game documents nothing more.

label: All selected
summary: Whether every item of the map editor's import tool is selected for import.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the 'Check/Uncheck All' box (tooltip 'Import All') at the top of the import tool's list.

label: Cancel import
summary: Closes the map editor's import tool without importing.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the tool's 'Cancel' button, which is disabled while an import runs. That it discards the loaded data is not shown.

label: Export mask picture
summary: The picture of the export mask, drawn over the heightmap in the import tool's workspace area.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the map editor import tool's 'Workspace Area' view, on top of the heightmap picture, drawn with GetMaskEffect. The game does not register its return type.

label: Export notes
summary: The notes that came with the export being imported, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it under 'Notes:' in the map editor's import tool, only when HasExportNotes is yes.

label: Heightmap picture
summary: The heightmap picture shown in the import tool's workspace area.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the map editor import tool's 'Workspace Area' view, drawn in greyscale with the export mask on top. The game does not register its return type.

label: Mask effect
summary: The drawing effect the import tool uses for the export mask picture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `effect` of the export mask picture in the map editor's import tool; the file notes that its shader is set in code. The game does not register its return type.

label: Has export notes
summary: Whether the export being imported came with notes.
details: Vanilla shows the 'Notes:' box of the map editor's import tool only when this is yes.

label: Import
summary: Imports the selected items into the affected area of the map, in the map editor's import tool.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Import' button, whose tooltip says it imports the selected items in the affected area. The tool warns that importing may take a while and the editor may freeze meanwhile.

label: Is importing
summary: Whether the map editor's import tool is importing right now.
details: Vanilla disables the tool's window and its Import, 'Show/Hide area on map' and Cancel buttons while this is yes.

label: Selection is mixed
summary: Whether only some of the import tool's items are selected, so the 'select all' box is neither fully on nor off.
details: Vanilla shows an extra mark on the 'Check/Uncheck All' box when this is yes. That this mark means a partly selected list is read from the name.

label: Zip loaded
summary: Whether the import tool has finished loading the zip file to import.
details: Vanilla shows a loading spinner while it is no, and the tool's content (workspace area, lists, buttons) once it is yes.

label: Refresh heightmap
summary: Probably reloads the heightmap shown in the import tool.
details: Going by its name. It belongs to the engine's internal GUI category, and nothing in the game uses it.

label: This tool
summary: The import tool itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name and the same name's common use elsewhere (as Character.Self inside other calls). Nothing here uses it on this type.

label: Show area on map
summary: Shows or hides the import tool's work area on the map, through the map editor's reference overlay.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Show/Hide area on map' button, so each click switches the overlay.

label: Toggle all selected
summary: Selects all items of the import tool, or clears them all.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the 'Check/Uncheck All' box of the map editor's import tool.
